Text: The adjusted statewide reporting context includes 140,706 students, 42 LEAs, 228 coded schools, and 5 vocational/program records without school codes. DAFB and Bryan Allen Stevenson School of Excellence are excluded from the reported totals.

The full proposed model allocates $2056.1M, compared with $1562.2M captured in the partial recreated current model, producing a gross modeled allocation difference of +$493.8M (+31.6%). Proposed Base and Central Office Funding totals $1614.0M, a difference of +$51.8M (+3.3%) before weighted funding is added.

All 42 included LEAs increase under the gross full-model comparison. The statewide gross increase is +31.6%. Across LEAs, the median increase is +39.6%, with the middle half ranging from +29.6% to +48.4%. Under the position-based comparison, 41 LEAs increase and 1 decrease. The statewide position-based change is +3.3%, while the median LEA change is +9.4%. All 23 included charter LEAs increase, while 1 of the 19 traditional districts decrease.

The full-model result is a gross modeled allocation difference, not a confirmed net increase in state spending. The current baseline remains incomplete, and current appropriations that may continue, be consolidated, or be replaced by Opportunity or Operational Funding have not yet been subtracted.
